To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the tools of economic analysis have rarely been employed to support decision-making regarding pediatric obesity in Germany, that this has been due to the fact that there are methodological problems in health-economic evaluations, that there are large knowledge gaps in this area and that the use of economic analysis is a necessary but not a sufficient condition to support decision-making in this field.
the tools of economic evaluation of interventions aimed at preventing pediatric obesity are not yet widely used in Germany.
health economic methods have not played a significant role in informing policy in Germany so far.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the tools of health economics can contribute to the development of effective policies for combating pediatric obesity.
the role of economic analysis in the design of health policy in the field of pediatric obesity in Germany.
the question of whether health economics can play a more important role than it has so far in informing German health policy and evaluating the outcomes in the area of pediatric obesity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, although health economics is an indispensible tool for the development of health policies and interventions, its use has been limited in this area so far.
health economics has not yet been a key policy instrument in combating pediatric obesity in Germany and other countries, but it should be.
the role of health economic methods in informing policy on combating pediatric obesity has been rather limited so far.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are in need of a more comprehensive approach to health economics and policy-making in this area.

health economics has not yet played a major role in informing German health policy on how to combat the pediatric obesity epidemic, although it has the potential to be an important tool for policy-makers in this area.
we have to find a way to integrate the results of economic analyses into a process of deliberative policy-making.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, despite the many unresolved issues, health economics should not be ignored in the fight against pediatric obesity.

health economics can make important contributions to policy development in the area of pediatric obesity, but that the role of health-economic analyses should be embedded in a more comprehensive process of policy deliberation.
the health-economic perspective should be included in the process of developing and evaluating strategies to prevent pediatric overweight and obesity in Germany.
